questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The reason why I choose Norway was because of the possibilities in the nature, such as wonderful hiking trips, skiing, Norden light and living with the Norwegians. Norway is an amazing place to visit but living there for half a year gives so much more of Norway that I haven't seen before. There are so many cute cities as well. 

The reason why I choose Norway was because of the possibilities in the nature, such as wonderful hiking trips, skiing, Norden light and living with the Norwegians. Norway is an amazing place to visit but living there for half a year gives so much more of Norway that I haven't seen before. There are so many cute cities as well. 

The reason why I choose university of South Eastern Norway (USN) was because there course about health promotion and management sounded interesting, and wasn't something you could study in Copenhagen. I was also considering a “friluftsliv” studie, but I thought that might be more fun just to do in my free time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In USN they have do a lot to make the students feel welcome and they arrange a lot of activities for the students, such as study nights with free food and soda, movies nights, parties, game nights and lots of others.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The website of USN is easy to understand, and use to find information about the studies. The website
SSN.no
gives a lot of information about housing and the area, studying tips and so on. Its a place with all the information you need as a student at USN. You can easily call them or send them an email if you should have any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You can always contact SSN or look at there website, they welcome you and give you a lot of information when you arrive. If you arrive in the summer, there are "faderuke", which is like "introuge" in Denmark. Where you meed a lot of other student and there a good parties as well, color run and trips to the beach. At campus Vestfold there is a lot of beachvolley. Your "fathers" (a tutor in danish) will also show you campus and where to find stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: At SSN you can choose between different housing. At campus Vestfold you can live at fagerlund, Klokkegården or Åsgårdstrand. I lived at Fagerlund and can really recommend Fagerlund. If you are in doubt you can call SSN and ask them what might fit you the best.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared kitchen with 14 other students, and I was the best. All ways someone to talk with and be with in the kitchen. There is plenty of space for you to cook as well. We had taco nights together every friday, and sometimes a party at our floor afterwards or at the other floors. I still had my on freezer, refrigerator and cupboard for kitchen utensils and food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Bring your own kitchen stuff, such as pans, plats and so on. You use your own stuff. So if you can transport it and bring some, then do that, so you don't have to buy it there. If you live other places, tjek that before you go.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was an easy registration process, you get the information step by step and they help you if there is anything you don't understand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can call them or look at their webpages. They email if they need information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The starting date of the course might be later then what it says, I got told it started the 16th, but it started at the end of august. But that just gave me time to meet people, go on trips and get used to campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the course "Exercise and Health Management" is good. Especially the pratical weeks was a great experience. I went to a place called Beitostolen Helsesportcenter, and work there for to weeks with a group of handicapped kids in the age between 8 and 12 years and did sports with them for 2 weeks. I can really recommend it. And the things you learn doing the course is something you use at the practical week.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was an easy and fun course. The English wasn't a problem. Its easier then at Copenhagen. But I just liked that, so I had more freetime to enjoy Norway.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had classes, where the teacher talk and then some group work, individual work, presentations and both an oral an written exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Exercise and Health Management. Which is 30 ECTS, the course is two courses: Physical activity, health promotion and project development - Physical activity, integration and life management.  
This program is a full time study programme and focus on benefits gained from being physically active in a life span cycle. Experiences from using physical activity as a tool to improve health in different Norwegian health and fitness contexts and in the work place will be covered. In addition, the courses will draw upon experiences from health promotive work carried out in different sports contexts to obtain better health in society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend that study for sports student or students who are interested in sport and teaching:
The Exercise and Health Management. Which is 30 ECTS, the course is two courses: Physical activity, health promotion and project development - Physical activity, integration and life management.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol is expensive in Norway. I did eat and drink good. I rented the books at the library, so I didn't pay for them. I used my 3 like home, so my parents paid for communication. I did a lot of trips, but with sleeping in tent and so on, so that wasn't expensive and I recommend it! I was friends with a lot of people with car, so it wasn't that often I took public transport, which can be expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, busses, trains and alcohol. Norway is just expensive. But nice quality!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of different sports activities at the campus in Vestfold, such as swimming, training center, volleyball, handball, climbing, running in the forest and basket.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The sports mentioned above, with the other students at campus. Its so much fun and a good way to make friends. Other then that movie night, game nights, parties, concerts and so on. A lot, so plenty to do. The international students had coffee meetings every Wednesday.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The volleyball, climbing, go on hikes, skiing, go see the norden light in Tromsø or Trondheim (we took airplane with the other international students).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing in Hemsedal! See the norden light in Tromsø or Trondheim in October to November. Do hikes at Trolltunga & Preikestolen, Galdhøpiggen & Knutshøe, Gjendebu Memurubu Gjendesheim, Ålesund & Rampestreken. Go to Bergen, Oslo and Kristiansand.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Its a lot like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the students activities, parties and sports. The Norweidians are sweet.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It took me two mounts to get really use to norwigien. Some words are opposite than Danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Living with norwigiens are fun and go see the nature and mountains!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go on trips!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring active clothes and hiking shoes!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The trips and living at the collective at campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At lære norsk.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
